title: Flexible Horseshoe Card public configuration
description: Public Flexible Horseshoe Card configuration contract plus authoring semantics and non-validating functional relationship metadata. v12 closes interpretation gaps found by AI authoring tests: FHS-local entities, JavaScript template context, sparkline selector applicability, slider interaction/scale semantics, SVG styling boundaries, and explicit final validation guidance.

template.description: Template reference merged into this configuration before normal runtime use.

embedded.description: Marks the card as embedded in another FHS/card context where supported.

constants.description: Card-level constants reusable through ref(name) and calc(expression).

styles.description: SVG/CSS style configuration for this item. In FHS text rendering the normal base font is 12 internal SVG units, equivalent to about 6 logical units on the standard 100-unit card; therefore 1em is approximately 6 logical units.

color_filter.description: Optional FHS color-filter configuration applied in the normal card/group/item filter cascade.

cards.description: Nested/child card definitions positioned by the parent FHS card.

aspectratio.description: Width/height aspect ratio. The normal 1/1 logical card is 100 x 100; an aspect ratio 2/1 produces a 200 x 100 logical canvas while retaining the same 100-unit reference scale.

card_filter.description: Card-level filter configuration retained for compatibility where supported.

entity_index.description: Index or named entity slot selecting one configured card entity for this item.

show.description: Visibility/mode selectors for this tool. Exact supported keys are tool-specific.

horseshoe_position.description: Horseshoe-specific position configuration retained inside the horseshoe tool.

horseshoe_scale.description: Scale/range configuration used to interpret entity values along this horseshoe.

horseshoe_state.description: State/progress rendering configuration for this horseshoe.

horseshoe_marker.description: Optional marker rendered on/around the horseshoe path.

horseshoe_background.description: Background rendering configuration for the horseshoe.

horseshoe_labels.description: Label rendering configuration for the horseshoe.

horseshoe_tickmarks.description: Tickmark rendering configuration for the horseshoe.

color_stops.description: FHS color-stop definition used to map numeric or string entity states to colors and optional styles.

colorstops.description: Normalized/runtime color-stop representation. Prefer public color_stops in authored YAML unless this field is explicitly documented for the containing feature.

bar_mode.description: Horseshoe progress interpretation mode, including normal and bidirectional variants.

radius.description: Radius used by this object. See the containing tool description for whether it is a normal FHS logical dimension or a legacy/raw SVG value.

tickmarks_radius.description: Radius used for horseshoe tickmark placement on the normal FHS logical scale.

arc_degrees.description: Angular extent in degrees. Positive and negative values follow the direction conventions of the containing tool.

start_angle.description: Starting angle in degrees for the path or gauge.

flip.description: Optional horizontal and/or vertical mirroring of the rendered item.

xpos.description: Horizontal position in FHS logical coordinates. A 1/1 card uses a 100-unit reference width: 0 is the left edge, 50 the center and 100 the right edge. Inside a group, 50 is the neutral local position: final_x = group.xpos + item.xpos - 50.

ypos.description: Vertical position in FHS logical coordinates. A 1/1 card uses a 100-unit reference height: 0 is the top edge, 50 the center and 100 the bottom edge. Inside a group, 50 is the neutral local position: final_y = group.ypos + item.ypos - 50.

yposc.description: Alternative vertical centre coordinate used by current FHS runtime. It uses the same 100-unit logical and group-local coordinate rules as ypos.

coordinate_system.name: FHS logical coordinate system
coordinate_system.standard_card: A 1/1 card is authored as a 100 x 100 logical canvas.
coordinate_system.origin: 0,0 is the top-left of the logical card; x grows right and y grows down.
coordinate_system.internal_svg: The runtime base SVG dimension is 200. Normal logical dimensions are converted with logical/100*200, so 1 logical unit = 2 internal SVG units.
coordinate_system.aspectratio: Aspect ratio multiplies the reference dimensions. 2/1 yields a 400 x 200 internal SVG viewBox, corresponding to a 200 x 100 logical canvas.

examples.description: Place an item one quarter from the left and halfway down

group_coordinates.design_reason: Groups use 50,50 as their local no-offset position so a newly grouped item remains visible at the group center. Authors can design grouped content around the middle instead of around 0,0 where part of it could fall outside the card.
group_coordinates.nested_groups: The same 50-centered formula is applied recursively to parent groups.

typography.rule: For normal FHS text, 1em corresponds to approximately 6 logical units on the standard 100-unit card; 2em is approximately 12 logical units.
typography.warning: CSS/em font sizes are not raw FHS width/height numbers. Do not interpret 1em as 1 logical unit.

dimension_spaces.fhs-logical: Positions and most geometry use the 100-unit logical reference scale.
dimension_spaces.raw-svg: A few legacy fields use internal SVG units directly; those fields are explicitly marked.
dimension_spaces.css-style: CSS/SVG style properties such as font-size and stroke-width use their own style semantics.
dimension_spaces.degrees: Rotation and angular path values are expressed in degrees.

authoring_guidance: Start ordinary 1/1 card placement from the 100 x 100 logical model.
When an item belongs to a group, design its local position around 50,50 rather than adding the item coordinates directly to the group coordinates.
Use schema descriptions and x-fhs-unit annotations to distinguish logical geometry from CSS/em sizes and legacy raw SVG values.
Prefer current fields over deprecated compatibility fields.
Treat JSON Schema structure as syntax, descriptions as field semantics, and x-fhs-relationships as the functional behavior graph between otherwise valid fields.
When modifying an existing valid FHS card, preserve its working structure and make the smallest change that satisfies the request instead of rebuilding it in another style.

Resolve inheritance and fallbacks before duplicating configuration. Entity-level color stops, actions, formatting and other shared configuration should be reused when the relationship graph says the item can consume them.

When a reusable color-stop model also defines the value domain, prefer the explicit object form with color_stops.scales.default plus colors; compact color-stop forms remain valid compatibility/authoring syntax.
Distinguish FHS-defined behavior from authoring choices: positions, spacing and visual balance may be reasonable design decisions even when no schema relationship mandates a specific value.
Treat the JavaScript template context as a documented runtime API. Do not invent context objects or members.
entities and states are different: entities is the FHS card entity list and includes FHS-local inputs; states is Home Assistant hass.states.
FHS visual tools render as SVG. Use SVG/CSS presentation semantics in styles; do not infer HTML layout semantics unless a specific FHS feature documents them.

state.meaning: Resolved state or selected attribute for the entity bound to the current item.
state.shape: scalar resolved state/attribute value; convert with Number(...) when numeric arithmetic is required

entity.meaning: Complete resolved entity bound to the current item.

entities.meaning: Resolved FHS card entity-state list in entities[] order.
entities.includes: Configured Home Assistant entities and configured FHS-local entities.
entities.usage: Use entities[index].state or entities[entity_slots.name[0]].state for card entities.
entities.shape: array of entity-like objects in root entities[] order

entity_slots.meaning: Mapping from configured slot names to entity indexes.
entity_slots.shape: object whose values are arrays of indexes

states.important: This is not an alias for entities. Do not assume browser-local FHS entities exist in states.
states.shape: object/map keyed by Home Assistant entity_id; values are HA state objects
states.reactivity: When a template reads a Home Assistant entity through states['domain.object_id'], also include that entity in the card entities list so its state changes trigger card updates.

hass.meaning: Home Assistant frontend hass object available to the card.

constants.meaning: Resolved card constants available to the template.
constants.shape: object matching the resolved card constants namespace

item.usage: Read current item configuration/context; do not mutate it as a persistence mechanism.

x-fhs-relationships.purpose: Non-validating runtime-parity metadata describing how public FHS fields select, activate, inherit, override, reference and constrain one another. v12 adds explicit cross-layer contracts for FHS-local entities, JavaScript context, slider metadata, and chart-family selectors.

path_notation.root: Paths are public FHS YAML paths.
path_notation.arrays: [] means any item in that public array.
path_notation.wildcards: * means any applicable normal layout section/item.
path_notation.concepts: Targets beginning with @ name a semantic capability rather than a literal YAML field.
path_notation.resolved: Targets beginning with @resolved- name the effective value after documented public inheritance/override/fallback rules are applied.
path_notation.alternatives: A|B in a path means the relation applies independently to either named public field.
path_notation.selectors: Square-bracket predicates such as layout.controls[type=slider] select items by configured field value.
path_notation.constant_paths: constants.<path> uses JavaScript-like dot traversal. Dots separate nested object properties and are not literal characters in top-level constant names.

vocabulary.provides: The source makes a value or capability available for another feature to consume.
vocabulary.requires: The source feature only has the described functional effect when the target capability/configuration is available. This is behavioral, not necessarily a schema error.
vocabulary.activates: The source value or state enables a behavior that otherwise remains inactive.
vocabulary.overrides: When both source and target are available, the source takes precedence.
vocabulary.fallback: The target is used when the source is absent or does not supply the needed value.
vocabulary.references: The source identifies another configured object/value by index, slot, id, section/id pair, or symbolic reference.
vocabulary.affects: The source changes interpretation, geometry, rendering, or behavior of the target without being a hard requirement.

relations.description: Selects the configured entity whose state/configuration is supplied to the layout item.
relations.resolution: Numeric indices address array position; named slot forms address the corresponding configured slot where supported.

relations.description: Creates a symbolic entity selector that can be used instead of relying only on numeric array positions.
Defines a reusable color-stop palette on an entity configuration. The palette is passive until a consuming visual mode activates color-stop behavior.
Defines color stops directly on a layout item for color-stop-aware rendering. SparklineGraphTool uses its separate nested sparkline.color_stops / sparkline.show interface.

Item-level color_stops take precedence over color stops inherited from the selected entity when both are present. SparklineGraphTool uses its separate nested sparkline.color_stops / sparkline.show interface.

When a color-stop-aware item has no local color_stops, it can consume the selected entity configuration color stops instead. SparklineGraphTool uses its separate nested sparkline.color_stops / sparkline.show interface.
For ordinary color-stop-aware layout tools, color-stop rendering is activated by item_style modes. SparklineGraphTool uses its separate nested sparkline.color_stops / sparkline.show interface.
relations.resolution: Resolve local layout item color_stops first, otherwise the selected entity color_stops.

relations.description: A color-stop item_style needs a resolved color-stop palette to produce color-dependent visual output. SparklineGraphTool uses its separate nested sparkline.color_stops / sparkline.show interface.
relations.effect_if_missing: Color-stop styling has no palette to consume; this relationship is not promoted to a JSON Schema validation error.

relations.description: For ordinary layout items that support the generic color-stop model, local color_stops can activate the default hard color-stop mode when item_style is omitted. SparklineGraphTool uses its separate nested sparkline.color_stops / sparkline.show interface.

The selected generic item_style chooses the same-named mode dictionary that controls whether the calculated color is applied to fill, stroke, or both. SparklineGraphTool uses its separate nested sparkline.color_stops / sparkline.show interface.
Color-dependent horseshoe_style modes activate the resolved horseshoe color-stop palette. Resolve local horseshoe color_stops first, otherwise the selected entity color_stops.
Color-dependent horseshoe_style modes need the resolved horseshoe color-stop palette to produce their intended color-dependent output.
relations.effect_if_missing: The selected color-stop style lacks its color source; this is behavior metadata rather than a schema constraint.

relations.description: Color-dependent scale_style modes consume the same resolved horseshoe color-stop palette as the state layer.
An explicit horseshoe_scale.min overrides the minimum supplied by the resolved color-stop scales.default for horseshoe geometry.
An explicit horseshoe_scale.max overrides the maximum supplied by the resolved color-stop scales.default for horseshoe geometry.
If horseshoe_scale.min is omitted, the resolved color-stop scales.default minimum is used when available; otherwise runtime falls back to 0.
If horseshoe_scale.max is omitted, the resolved color-stop scales.default maximum is used when available; otherwise runtime falls back to 100.
Maps non-numeric/string entity states into values or levels used by horseshoe state rendering and color selection where configured.
A state_value mapping can convert textual entity states into numeric values before color-stop selection.
same_as inherits an earlier item in the same layout section by id.
Fields supplied on the same_as item override inherited values; nested object overrides may be partial because configuration merging is deep.
Marks inherited paths that must be replaced instead of deep-merged during same_as compilation.
Adds a static numeric delta to the inherited value of the corresponding known numeric field after same_as inheritance.
Uses the measured geometry of another layout item to size/fit a rectangle; padding expands that measured geometry.
Object-form width/height item references reuse measured dimensions from another layout item.
Assigns a layout item to the named group and therefore to that group local coordinate frame.
Grouped items use the group-local 50,50 neutral position. Final position is group position plus item position minus 50 on each axis.
Nested groups recursively use the same 50-centered local-coordinate rule after resolving their parent group.
Applies the named clip definition to the rendered layout item.
A mask string references one named mask. A mask array references multiple masks that are applied as nested masks in configured order.
soft_arc derives its fade geometry from the first arc in the referenced clip definition.
relations.resolution: The referenced clip must exist and supply arcs[0]; the runtime expands soft_arc into separate edge and chord masks.

relations.description: Selects the animation/style entry used for that layout item.
Item color_filter participates after card and group filters in the render cascade.
A group color_filter participates in the color-filter cascade for items in that group, including ancestor group chains.

ref(path) resolves a whole-value static reference through card constants. Dot notation traverses nested object properties using JavaScript-style identifier segments; arrays are not traversed by index.
relations.resolution: The resolved scalar is inserted directly. Resolved objects and arrays are deep-cloned so each ref() insertion is independent.

relations.description: calc() may use numeric top-level constants and nested numeric object paths that are already available in declaration order. Non-numeric leaves and arrays are not exposed to the calc scope.
relations.resolution: calc() evaluates once at the configuration boundary and must return a finite number. Later constants may use earlier numeric constants/namespaces.

relations.description: Root, entity and tool template fields select an FHS template and optionally supply variables before normal runtime use.
When attribute is configured, entity-bound display tools use that Home Assistant attribute value instead of the entity state.
Provides the configured display name consumed by entity-name aware tools instead of relying only on the Home Assistant friendly name.
Provides an explicit icon source for entity-icon aware tools; otherwise they may derive the icon from Home Assistant entity metadata.
An explicit entity unit replaces the unit returned by Home Assistant formatting for FHS state/UOM display.
Provides the default minimum and maximum fractional precision for numeric StateTool formatting unless a state format override supplies a more specific bound.
Provides default state formatting options for state-derived text when the layout state item does not supply its own format object.
An item-level state format object takes precedence over the selected entity format object for that state item.
decimals_min overrides the minimum fractional digits otherwise supplied by entities[].decimals or Home Assistant precision.
decimals_max overrides the maximum fractional digits otherwise supplied by entities[].decimals or Home Assistant precision.
The end, top and bottom modes render the resolved unit of measurement with the state; none suppresses it. top/bottom create a vertical state+UOM layout.
The uom block styles and offsets the UOM that is made visible by show.uom; it does not by itself select whether the UOM is shown.
State mappings can translate textual/entity states into display values or labels used by StateTool in addition to their color-stop input role.
A gesture action configured on a layout item takes precedence over the same gesture action on the selected entity configuration.
When an entity-bound layout item omits a gesture action, FHS uses the corresponding action from the selected entity when configured.
For an entity-bound item with neither item-level nor entity-level tap_action, the normal tap fallback is Home Assistant more-info when a valid Home Assistant target exists.
An entity explicitly supplied inside an action overrides the entity target inferred from the item entity_index for that action.
The default scale travels with an entity color-stop model and provides its reusable value domain to consumers that use the entity palette.
An item-local color-stop default scale provides the value domain that travels with the item-local palette.
A horseshoe-local color_stops model takes precedence over the color-stop model supplied by its selected entity.
When a horseshoe does not define local color_stops, its resolved color-stop model can come from the selected entity configuration.
The scales.default embedded in the resolved horseshoe color-stop model supplies the default min/max range before explicit horseshoe_scale min/max overrides are applied.
A horseshoe_background block is rendered only when show.horseshoe_background selects a background mode instead of none.
Color-stop/gradient horseshoe background modes consume the resolved horseshoe color-stop palette.
When horseshoe_background.width is omitted, the background uses horseshoe_scale.width.
state_progress controls whether the filled/current-value state path is rendered.
state_marker controls whether the marker at the current value is rendered; a useful default path marker exists even without an explicit horseshoe_marker block.
For a path-attached marker, size defaults to horseshoe_state.width when no explicit marker size is supplied.
Without explicit marker styles, the marker follows the current horseshoe state appearance, including state color behavior.
labels_at selects where configured horseshoe labels are rendered; none leaves the label layer inactive.
stringstate_mode and stringstate_level need a state map that translates source states into their segment/level semantics.
A state_map on the horseshoe item takes precedence over a state_map nested inside horseshoe_state.
If the horseshoe item has no state_map, FHS can use horseshoe_state.state_map instead.
Spline scale types require the corresponding spline definition to map values along the path.
bar_mode changes how progress grows around zero/the path, including normal, bidirectional and absolute behaviors.
When zero_ratio is omitted, FHS derives the zero position from the resolved horseshoe scale; symmetrical bidirectional modes use the midpoint.
A group parent names another configured group; omitted parent means the implicit card root.
Group visibility cascades through the parent chain. A hidden ancestor keeps every descendant hidden even when the child itself is visible.
visibility:hidden suppresses visible/pointer rendering but keeps the tool in normal lifecycle/measurement behavior.
A group scale contributes to the render transform of items assigned to that group.
flip mirrors the rendered item on x, y or both axes and combines with its resolved group scale.
dzpos is added to the resolved/default zpos to determine the final layer position.
The top-level type discriminator selects the toggle, select, number, button or slider control behavior and its matching public configuration.
A toggle item_style selects the same-named visual configuration, such as ha, ios or industrial.
Select item_viz chooses the visualization block, currently viz_button or viz_line.
When option_map is omitted, the select control derives its selectable options from the bound entity options.
Each explicit select option inherits the corresponding control gesture action when that option does not override it.
Inside select-option action configuration, an exact option(path) reference is replaced with that option field while preserving its datatype.
Slider item_viz selects the matching visualization block, currently linear or circular.
A range slider binds exactly two value channels through values[].
Each slider value channel can bind its own entity; range sliders use the two bound entities as lower and upper values.
Object-form slider scale entries such as {attribute: min} read min/max/step metadata from the first slider value entity.
Visible slider values are rendered through normal StateTool semantics, so nested value.state can control state/UOM formatting and styles.
Each sparkline series may select its own configured entity independently from the coordinator sparkline item.
Entity-derived multipart text parts can select the entity whose name/area/state/unit semantics they render.
Each top-level constant name creates one addressable root for ref() and calc().
Constants are compiled in declaration order; a later constant can calculate from earlier numeric constants or nested numeric namespaces, not from a later declaration.
When the referenced value is an object or array, FHS deep-clones it before insertion so separate ref() uses can be modified independently.
Static calc exposes sin, cos, tan, abs, round, floor, ceil, min, max, sqrt and PI in addition to numeric constants.
relations.resolution: calc expressions must resolve to a finite number.

relations.description: Static ref()/calc() syntax replaces the whole configured value; FHS does not perform substring interpolation inside arbitrary strings.
A style paint value gradient(name) references a card-scoped layout gradient. Use gradient(name), not a raw url(#name), because runtime SVG ids are card-scoped.
gradientUnits controls numeric coordinate interpretation: objectBoundingBox numbers are percentages 0..100; userSpaceOnUse numbers are FHS logical dimensions converted to SVG units.
Numeric gradient stop offsets are FHS percentages: 0 is 0%, 50 is 50%, 100 is 100%.
Multiple configured masks are nested in array order; every mask constrains the result of the previous mask rather than being painted into one combined mask.
FHS first nests configured masks and then wraps the masked result in the configured clip path.
A soft_arc mask needs the first arc geometry of its referenced clip to derive edge and chord fades.
A clip/mask shape using dxpos or dypos is resolved relative to each consuming item, so FHS renders an item-specific SVG definition id.
When actions[] is supplied, configured actions execute sequentially in array order.
A perform-action action uses perform_action as the domain.service identifier.
A call-service action uses service as the domain.service identifier.
A navigate action consumes navigation_path; navigation_replace chooses replaceState instead of pushState.
A url action opens url_path in a new browser target.
A select-option action submits option to the bound select/input_select/number-compatible target.
When a bound entity configuration has source_entity_index, item/entity actions target that source entity unless the action explicitly supplies entity.
The local decrement shorthand is accepted by number-control minus buttons and translated at setState to a perform-action on the bound entity domain.
The local increment shorthand is accepted by number-control plus buttons and translated at setState to a perform-action on the bound entity domain.
Slider-local set-value is translated to perform-action on the active bound entity with data.value set to the current slider value.
For a custom slider action, value_field is a dotted destination path that receives the current active slider value before execution.
For a range slider, value_fields maps destination paths to lower or upper so both current values can be inserted into a custom action.
Graph selectors and chart-family configuration live inside the nested sparkline block. period, x_axis, y_axis and series remain at the sparkline item root.
chart_type is the primary graph-family discriminator and activates the matching nested graph-family configuration.
For chart_type radial, chart_variant must be line, area or dots and selects that presentation family.
For radial_barcode, chart_viz selects the rendered interval/segment shape and works together with chart_variant.
period.type selects calendar, rolling_window or real_time behavior. Historical types consume their matching nested branch; real_time has no history duration.
Current history and graph runtime reads duration.hour directly. Express multi-day windows in hours.
Historical bins determine the shared time-bucket resolution used by graph geometry, ticks and pointer buckets.
When per_hour is auto, FHS derives a concrete density from available graph width/radial arc length, chart family, history duration and bins.density.
Enables X grid rendering when the selected chart family exposes an X axis.
Enables Y grid rendering when the selected chart family exposes a Y axis.
Shows the X-axis path when the selected chart family exposes an X axis.
Shows the Y-axis path when the active series chart family exposes a Y axis.
Shows X tick marks when the selected chart family exposes an X axis. This toggle is independent of show.axis.x.
Shows Y tick marks when the active series chart family exposes a Y axis. This toggle is independent of show.axis.y.
Shows calculated X/time labels when the selected chart family exposes an X axis. This toggle is independent of show.axis.x.
Shows calculated Y/value/state labels when the active series chart family exposes a Y axis. This toggle is independent of show.axis.y.
Chart family limits which axis layers can render: line/area/bar/dots/equalizer/state_bands/radial support X+Y; barcode/radial_barcode support X only; graded supports neither.
x_axis config supplies axis, grid, tick and label styling/spacing for enabled X layers; configuring it does not itself show those layers.
y_axis config supplies bounds, axis, grid, tick and label styling/spacing for enabled Y layers; configuring it does not itself show those layers.
show.legend activates legend measurement/rendering and reserves graph area.
Legend position controls orientation and which side of the sparkline viewport is reserved for the legend.
show.day_night activates auxiliary sun/day-night history and the configured background/band visualization.
Day/night rendering requires calendar or rolling_window history and is rejected for real_time.
With a calendar period, day/night rendering does not support a positive future offset.
For line/area and radial line/area presentations, show.line controls whether the line path is retained/rendered.
show.points adds point geometry for compatible line/area/radial presentations.
line.show_dots adds dots even when the chart family itself is line.
area.show_dots adds dots to an area presentation.
show.fill selects solid versus fade fill treatment for fill-capable graph rendering.
Enables the line minimum/maximum envelope configuration.
Enables the area minimum/maximum envelope configuration.
For radial families, show.background controls the configured radial plot/background layer.
state_bands maps categorical history rows through sparkline.state_map for band levels/labels.
When chart_type is state_bands, runtime forces hard color-stop transitions because states are discrete.
Every explicit series starts from the complete normalized parent sparkline configuration and deep-merges its own overrides.
An explicit series may override the parent chart_type with line, area, dots, bar or radial.
A radial series may override the inherited line/area/dots chart_variant.
A series-wide item_style replaces the inherited shared paint choice unless a deeper line/area/minmax item_style is explicitly configured.
y_axis_id assigns the series to the primary or secondary shared Y-axis group; the default is primary.
An explicit series may override only the offset of the parent-selected calendar/rolling_window period branch; duration and bins stay parent-owned.
Radial series cannot be mixed with cartesian series, and the parent chart_type must be radial when all explicit series are radial.
Radial geometry is parent-owned and shared by radial series; runtime rejects a series-local sparkline.radial block.
relations.resolution: Configure radial geometry only on the parent sparkline.

relations.description: Explicit multi-series items support line, area, dots, bar and radial chart types; equalizer/graded/barcode/state_bands/radial_barcode are parent/single-series families.
A horseshoe with show.horseshoe false is filtered out during tool creation; true/default keeps the gauge active.
show.tickmarks is the primary tickmark visibility selector. A boolean controls both layers; {major, minor} controls them independently.
Legacy show.ticks is consulted only when show.tickmarks is absent.
Legacy scale_tickmarks: true can synthesize major tickmark geometry from horseshoe_scale when no explicit major/minor tickmark block exists.
labels_at selects where horseshoe labels are generated. The default none keeps the label layer inactive.
String-state modes select the matching horseshoe_labels.stringstate_mode or stringstate_level configuration.
path.type selects the generic path generator. Current families are arc, line, rectangle, polygon, wave, spiral and infinity.
A center-attached marker represents a pointer from the path center and requires an explicit icon.
A center-attached marker is valid only for an arc path.
Marker icon and shape are mutually exclusive; configure one visual source, not both.
For attach_to: path, if neither icon nor shape is supplied, the marker defaults to a circle.
absolute bar mode requires scale min <= 0 and max > 0.
absolute bar mode uses the physical path start as zero and rejects an explicit zero_ratio.
bidirectional and bidirectional_symmetrical default zero_ratio to 0.5 when it is not explicitly supplied.
Other non-absolute modes derive the zero position from horseshoe_scale min/max when zero_ratio is omitted.
Gradient horseshoe styles used with bidirectional/absolute ranges spanning zero require color stops on the needed negative and positive sides.
show.item_viz selects the matching nested linear or circular visualization block.
For item_variant single, runtime creates one internal value binding from the slider's entity_index.
For item_variant range, runtime uses the first of the two values as the slider's primary entity_index.
value.show controls creation/rendering of StateTool value labels; value.position/gap/offset then place them.
Current number control supports the stepper variant.
Current number control supports the buttons visualization.
content.mode selects the horizontal or vertical number-control content layout; each layout owns minus, value and plus subconfiguration.
Defines the public color-stop palette for sparkline graph rendering; BaseTool normalizes it into sparkline.colorstops at the runtime-config boundary.
Sparkline item_style color modes select how the graph consumes its color stops.

fhs_input_number, fhs_input_boolean and fhs_input_select are domains. A configured local entity must use domain.object_id, for example fhs_input_number.horseshoe_width; the bare domain is not an entity id.
FHS-local inputs are ordinary entity entries in the card entities list. Do not create nested fhs_input_number/fhs_input_boolean/fhs_input_select blocks under controls.
A bound fhs_input_number exposes its configured numeric metadata to number and slider controls.
Controls bind FHS-local inputs through the same entity_index mechanism as other configured card entities.
Browser-local FHS entities participate in the card entity-state list and can be read from JavaScript through entities[index].state.
JavaScript states refers specifically to the Home Assistant state registry. It is not an alias for the FHS card entities list.
JavaScript entities is the resolved FHS card entity-state list in configured order.
A runtime JavaScript template returns the complete value for its containing field and must satisfy that field's documented value/type semantics.
Slider interaction owns update_interval and haptic behavior. Numeric step belongs to slider.scale.step or the bound entity's step metadata.
When explicit slider scale values are absent, runtime resolves min/max/step from attributes of the primary bound entity.
For chart_type barcode, static chart_variant is audio, stalactites or stalagmites; otherwise omit it.
For chart_type graded, the documented static chart_variant is rank_order.
For radial_barcode, chart_variant is fixed, sunburst, sunburst_centered, sunburst_outward or sunburst_inward.
For radial_barcode, chart_viz is bar, flower, flower2 or rice_grain.
Do not emit chart_variant or chart_viz for a chart family that does not define that selector. Omit the field instead of inventing values such as default, none or standard.
FHS visual tools render as SVG. General SVG/CSS presentation semantics may be used inside style dictionaries, but this does not authorize HTML-only layout assumptions or new FHS configuration fields.
When JavaScript reads a Home Assistant entity through states, include that entity in the card entities list so Home Assistant state changes participate in the card update lifecycle.

card.animations.description: Public FHS schema definition for card animations.

card.cards.description: Public FHS schema definition for card cards.

card.colorFilter.description: Public FHS schema definition for card colorFilter.

entity.description: Entity id in normal domain.object_id form. Home Assistant entities use their HA domain (for example sensor.living_room_temperature). unit.description: Unit-of-measurement override for the configured entity.

decimals.description: Number of decimal places used for numeric display formatting.

convert.description: Named FHS state converter applied before final display formatting.

layout.textOverflowFit.description: Public FHS schema definition for layout textOverflowFit.

layout.vlines.description: Public FHS schema definition for layout vlines.
